$comment: All tunable game rules live here. Nothing in src/ hardcodes these numbers. Edit, restart, done. See README 'Tuning the config'.

scoring.$comment: A correct answer is worth 'correct' at the buzzer and 'correct + speedBonus' if you answer instantly, decaying between the two. The floor matters: a slow correct answer must still beat abstaining, so the bonus is added on top rather than decayed down to zero.

speed.$comment: fullBonusMs pays the whole bonus for answers inside it — you have to read the question first, and 300ms vs 900ms is recognition, not speed. After that the bonus decays to zero at the deadline. 'linear' is a straight ramp; 'ease-out' holds value longer early and drops away fast at the end.

timing.$comment: answerWindowMs is the fair, synchronised per-question clock. It starts only once both clients have acknowledged the (face-down) question AND at a shared wall-clock instant both clients agree on.
timing.$untimed: With the per-question timer switched off, a question closes only once BOTH players have answered — so untimedBackstopMs is a safety valve, not a game rule: it stops one player walking away from freezing the match forever. Make it generous. The speed bonus still decays over answerWindowMs either way; past that you simply score the floor instead of being cut off.

suddenDeath.$comment: Played one question at a time from the same category until the tie breaks. Mix is sampled from this weighting; questions used in the main 20 are never reused inside the same match.

selection.$comment: tierShortfallPolicy decides what happens when a tier cannot be filled with UNSEEN questions. 'prefer-fresh' spills into an adjacent tier's unseen pool first (keeps questions new, bends the difficulty mix). 'prefer-difficulty' recycles already-seen questions at the correct tier first (keeps the mix exact, repeats questions). Business hard has only 41 questions, so a 'tough' Business match hits this after 3 matches.

room.$comment: Alphabet omits characters that are ambiguous when read aloud over a call or typed on a phone keyboard: B/8, I/1/L, O/0/Q, S/5, Z/2.
